# Blocking-thread cap measurement

Measurement only; never for upstream.

Phase 1 is one Linux hosted job, on pushes to `bench/blocking-threads` in the measurement fork only. No Rust build, repository dependency install, default-branch change or pull request. macOS and Windows are gated on the Linux result; their measurement helpers are retained but no workflow starts them.

Released `@rspack/core@2.2.8`, Node 24. A public synthetic 20,000-module binary tree makes all 1-3 KiB sources reachable, with 300 generated resolver packages. Development mode, cheap module source maps, no persistent cache. SingleCompiler and client/server MultiCompiler share the same source fixture. Every launch is a new process. Caps unset (default 4), 16 and 64 rotate ABC/BCA/CAB across five paired rounds; 512 runs once after each cell as an unpaired reference. A fifth round can be omitted with an explicit record to respect the 115-minute job limit. All variants and read delays execute sequentially.

The prior cache slow-disk study's 14-GiB direct-I/O loop file, dm-delay and ext4 data=ordered stack is reused, including zero-delay. The entire fixture, including generated node_modules, is copied with cp -a onto the mapper. Added read latency is 0, 2 or 8 ms; writes have no added latency. Before every launch, sync, global drop_caches and a mincore check require zero fixture page residency. The probe does not read file contents but does visit metadata. Package/binding installation and outputs remain on normal storage. Failure to provide dm-delay, direct I/O, 512-byte sectors or the previous ext4 backing filesystem stops the study rather than substituting a disk setup.

Timing and CPU start at run() and end at its callback. Make spans make through finishMake. Stats timings are retained. JS samples RSS and Linux proc memory every 100 ms; an external sampler also records Linux VmHWM, RssAnon, VmSwap and thread counts. END is captured immediately after the callback and 12 s later, without GC or compiler close. The compiler remains alive until after END(12 s), then closes. This isolates the 10 s blocking-thread keep-alive, not a long-running watch steady state. VmHWM is the process-lifetime peak, including initialization; sampled RssAnon can miss short peaks.

A stdin handshake starts the compiler after external sampling begins. Maximum observed threads must increase for caps 4, 16, 64 in each cell to establish env effectiveness. Thread counts include Node, Rayon and other native threads, not just the blocking pool. 512 is a lazy upper bound and need not spawn 512 threads. Output SHA-256 must match across every arm and round within a cell. A failed launch is recorded and stops the job; it is never a sample. Raw data, samples, cold residency, package lock, disk and runner environment are uploaded even on failure.
